design_rationale: The study is described as an investigator-blinded, randomized controlled trial where participants were assigned to intervention or control groups using a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated concealed sequence was prepared, eight participants were incorrectly randomized due to study coordinator errors, raising some concerns about allocation integrity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was completed via a computer-generated randomization list issued by a statistician with block sizes of 10 and concealed from the recruitment coordinator until randomization... Six participants were incorrectly randomized to the intervention and two to the control explaining the imbalance. These mistakes in randomization displayed no pattern and were the results of acknowledged study coordinator error. Each participant was analysed according to the group they were ultimately randomized to by the research coordinator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Parents were aware of the assigned intervention and a large proportion of the control arm (about 45%) used emollients regularly, representing potential contamination/deviations from protocol that could affect the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intervention arm was supplied with Cetaphil® Restoraderm®... The control arm was given no specific instructions regarding use of emollients except to use emollients of their choice on an as needed basis... At 2, 6 and 12 months, the intervention group had 87%, 72.4% and 66.7% high adherence, respectively, vs. 45.2%, 45.8% and 45.5% in the control group... The primary clinical end point analysis was conducted on an intent-to-treat basis using a complete case approach...

domain_judgments.rationale: A substantial proportion of participants (28%) had missing outcome data at 12 months, and the analysis was restricted to complete cases without evidence that missingness was independent of outcome status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Less than half the target sample size was enrolled (n = 100, goal sample was 208) with 28% lost to follow-up... The primary clinical end point analysis was conducted on an intent-to-treat basis using a complete case approach and statistical analysis completed through chi-square test of two proportions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed using standard validated diagnostic criteria by trained investigators blinded to intervention allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of AD at 12 months diagnosed by a blinded investigator (‘Investigatorconfirmed AD’). The criteria for the development of AD were the U.K. Working Party Criteria adapted to identify incident cases of AD rather than a 12-month period prevalence.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of an accessible pre-specified analysis plan or trial registration protocol, and post hoc analyses were introduced following substantial dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the large dropout rate, a post hoc secondary analysis of the primary outcome was also performed using the cumulative incidence of AD diagnosed by any of the following – a blinded investigator, non-investigator physician or provider-diagnosed AD recorded in the medical record in the first 12 and 24 months (‘any AD’).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by a substantial 28% loss to follow-up for the primary outcome analyzed via complete case analysis (Domain 3), accompanied by concerns regarding coordinator errors during randomization and protocol deviations/contamination in the control arm.

paper_title: 3762c968_Br J Dermatol - 2017 - Lowe - A randomized trial of a barrier lipid replacement strategy for the prevention of atopic
design_rationale: The study is described as a 'pilot randomized, parallel, single-blind (outcome assessor), controlled trial' with a randomization sequence developed by a biostatistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a randomization sequence was developed and baseline characteristics were reported to be balanced, the specific method of sequence generation and allocation concealment mechanism are not detailed in the text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We thank Dr Lyle Gurrin, University of Melbourne, for assistance with developing the randomization sequence... The groups were well balanced on a range of baseline factors.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses were conducted on an intention-to-treat basis, and deviations such as co-intervention use were tracked without evidence of substantial implementation failures that would compromise the ITT effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intention-to-treat analysis showed no significant effect of routine barrier lipid replacement in early life on AD or sensitization outcomes... Use of other emollients (not study treatment) for on average ≥ 3 days per week during the intervention period occurred in 39% of the control group and 18% of the intervention group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for nearly all 80 recruited participants across follow-up time points (e.g. 73-77 assessed at 6 and 12 months).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 1306 infants were screened and 80 were recruited... There was minimal loss to follow-up at each time point (Appendix S1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed by a blinded investigator using standardized diagnostic criteria and objective skin prick tests.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical follow-up of infants by a blinded assessor (C.A.) occurred at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months of age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The reported outcomes reflect the pre-specified primary clinical and allergic sensitization end points at all follow-up time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intention-to-treat analysis showed no significant effect of routine barrier lipid replacement in early life on AD or sensitization outcomes. However, there was a trend towards reduced risks of AD and food sensitization in the intervention group at 6 and 12 months of age (Table 1 and Appendix S1).

overall_summary: The trial has an overall risk of bias of some concerns driven by Domain 1, as the specific method of random sequence generation and allocation concealment was not fully detailed in the letter format. All other domains (deviations, missing data, outcome measurement with blinded assessors, and reporting) were judged to be at low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to emollient or control using a computer-generated pseudo-random sequence with permuted blocks via an internet-based central system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central computer-generated pseudo-random allocation sequence with concealed allocation via an internet-based system was implemented, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomisation schedule was created by the CTU using computer-generated pseudo-random code with permuted blocks of randomly varying size. The sequence was known only to the programmer until database lock. Research nurses randomly assigned participants to groups using a secure, internet-based randomisation system developed and maintained by the CTU.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although parents were unblinded, the trial evaluated a pragmatic recommendation/policy, contamination was modest, deviations were consistent with clinical practice, and an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We analysed participants as randomised regardless of adherence with allocation and using observed data... Sensitivity analyses were done using multiple imputation for missing data to include all participants in the analysis... and actual emollient use (complier average causal effect [CACE] accounting for emollient use in both groups).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were obtained for 87% of randomized infants, missingness was balanced across arms (14% vs 13%), and multiple imputation sensitivity analyses produced consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At age 2 years, eczema was present in 139 (23%) of 598 infants with outcome data collected in the emollient group and 150 (25%) of 612 infants in the control group... Sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary analysis, by use of data from GP records for missing primary outcome data, imputed missing data...

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were masked research nurses evaluating infants using validated diagnostic criteria, with accidental unmasking occurring in only 3% of cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was diagnosis of eczema over the past year (defined by the UK working party refinement of the Hanifin and Rajka diagnostic criteria for eczema) assessed by research nurses masked to treatment allocation at age 2 years.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered with a detailed published protocol and pre-specified statistical analysis plan, and reported all primary and secondary outcomes accordingly.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis and publication of data for the 2-year primary outcome timepoint were preplanned... The trial was registered at the ISRCTN registry before initiation of recruitment, ISRCTN21528841. For the statistical analysis plan see https://www.nottingham ac.uk/research/groups/cebd/ documents/researchdocs/0935- beep-sap-final-v1.0-20181205- signed.pdf

overall_summary: The trial was conducted with rigorous methodology, including concealed central randomization, blinded outcome assessment using validated diagnostic criteria, low and balanced attrition with robust sensitivity analyses, and complete reporting according to a prospective pre-specified analysis plan, resulting in a low risk of bias overall.

design_rationale: The study is a 2x2 factorial, multicentre, cluster-randomised trial where participants were randomly allocated to one of four groups using computer-generated cluster randomisation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated with cluster randomisation based on geography and time blocks, and baseline characteristics across groups were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using computergenerated cluster randomisation based on 92 geographical living area blocks as well as eight 3-month time blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be masked given the nature of the interventions, an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis was performed, and deviations reflected real-world practice without indication of systematic bias affecting the trial context.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study design did not allow for masking of study participants to the interventions. ... The primary eficacy analyses was done by intention-to-treat analysis on all randomly assigned participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for the vast majority of participants (>90% overall), missingness was addressed through prespecified sensitivity analyses including multiple imputation, and conclusions remained robust.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data for the primary endpoint were missing in 24 (4%) of 596 infants in the no intervention group, 76 (13%) of 575 in the skin intervention group, 45 (7%) of 642 in the food intervention group, and 79 (14%) of 583 in the combined intervention group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were masked to group allocation, established standardized diagnostic criteria (UK Working Party and Hanifin and Rajka) were used, and precautions were taken to avoid unmasking during examinations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To limit the risk of observer bias, study personnel who did the clinical follow-up investigations did not have access to the randomisation lists. Furthermore, parents were firmly instructed not to apply any type of emollient bath additives or leave-on emollients within 24 h before each follow-up investigation and all clinical assessments and investigations were done and recorded without knowledge of the group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, an analysis plan was finalized prior to unmasking, and outcomes were reported in accordance with prespecified analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was prespecified in the protocol, while the sensitivity analyses were specified in the SAP prior to any analyses and unmasking of the randomisation. ... The study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02449850.

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted, cluster-randomised trial with robust randomization, masked outcome assessment using validated diagnostic criteria, low and well-accounted-for missing data, and adherence to a prespecified statistical analysis plan, resulting in an overall low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial in which infants were randomly assigned to one of four groups using computerized random numbers generated with a minimization technique at a central location.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated centrally using computerized random numbers and minimization, ensuring allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intervention group allocation was determined by a randomization system based on the minimization technique (Nouvelle Place Inc., Tokyo, Japan). Babies born at term were randomized into 4 groups according to gender (male or female), mode of delivery (vaginal or Caesarean) and family history of allergic diseases (present or absent) using computerized random numbers. Randomization was performed at a central location.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label without blinding of participants or parents, control participants were allowed to apply emollients at their discretion (contamination/cross-over), and the primary analysis excluded participants with missing post-randomization data rather than performing a standard intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The control group was not prevented from applying emollients due to ethical reasons... As this could mask the effect of the moisturizer used as an intervention, we looked at the effect of any emollient (irrespective of the formal intervention assigned) on the development of AD.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 16.4% (90 of 549) of randomized infants were excluded from the primary outcome assessment due to missing data/loss to follow-up, and no imputation or sensitivity analysis was conducted to establish robustness to potential missingness bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the recruited participants, 549 babies qualified to be randomized... A total of 459 babies from the 4 groups completed the intervention and qualified for assessment of the primary outcome at 1 year of age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was based on parent-completed questionnaires in an unblinded open-label trial, meaning the outcome assessors (parents) were aware of the assigned intervention, potentially influencing parental reporting of symptoms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: AD was diagnosed according to the criteria of the Japanese Dermatological Association, when an itchy rash lasting 2 or more months was reported in the questionnaires returned at 1, 6, and 9 months and 1 year of the baby’s age. In addition, AD was diagnosed using the U. K. Working Party’s Diagnostic Criteria included in the questionnaire at 1 year.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered (UMIN000010838), and the reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with the prespecified endpoints and analysis procedures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the incidence of AD up to 1 year of age. The primary endpoint was analyzed by using a closed testing procedure for multiple comparisons of treatment.

overall_summary: The trial is judged as having some concerns overall due to potential bias from deviations from intended interventions (unblinded, permitted co-interventions in control group), missing outcome data (~16% attrition post-randomization without full ITT), and potential subjectivity in parent-reported primary outcome questionnaires in an open-label setting.

paper_title: a04e782a_The Journal of Dermatology - 2017 - Yonezawa - Effects of moisturizing skincare on skin barrier function and the prevention
design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial with individual allocation using block randomization stratified by gestational age and birth weight via central registration.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization used central registration with blocked and stratified sequences, and baseline characteristics were reasonably balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed individually according to central registration after measuring the skin barrier function at baseline. The randomization sequence used two or four blocks and was stratified according to whether the newborns were term and weighed more than 2500 g. The allocation ratio was 1:1.

domain_judgments.rationale: Parents were unblinded to assignment and non-protocol interventions/deviations were explicitly permitted (controls used lotion, intervention participants bathed daily), which could affect outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the intervention group, if parents were resistant to reducing the frequency of bathing, they were allowed to bathe their newborn daily, but they could only use soap every other day. In the control group, parents were allowed to apply a moisturizer to their newborns if they wanted to.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was low (11% overall; 96/113 analyzed in intervention and 106/114 in control for barrier function), with balanced dropouts and documented reasons unlikely to be related to true outcome status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, we analyzed the data of 202 infants (89.0%). Figure 1 shows a flow diagram of the enrollment procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Measurers of skin barrier function and parents evaluating daily skin problem diaries were not blinded to group assignment, which introduces potential detection bias particularly for parent-reported subjective skin conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, we could not blind the measurer or avoid bias among the parents who evaluated the infants' skin problems.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered (UMIN000013260) and reported outcomes aligned with pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000013260).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by unblinded outcome assessment (including parent-reported diary evaluations of skin problems) and allowable deviations from the intended skincare protocols across groups.
